name: Ahuzzam
title: Son of Ashhur and Naarah, descendant of Judah
summary: Ahussam is mentioned in 1 Chronicles 4:6 as one of the sons of Ashhur and his wife Naarah. Ashhur is regarded as the founder of the city of Tekoa in the hill country of Judah. Ahussam thus belongs to the tribe of Judah and is included in the detailed genealogies that link family lines to geographical settlements in Judah. Although the Bible tells us nothing more about his life or deeds, his place in the genealogy underscores the importance placed on preserving tribal lineages, which had practical significance for land distribution, inheritance rights, and identity. Tekoa, the city founded by his father, later became known, among other things, as the home of the prophet Amos.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the genealogy of Judah
keyEvents.description: Ahuzzam is mentioned as one of the sons of Ashhur and his wife Naarah in the record of the descendants of the tribe of Judah. Ashhur had two wives—Naarah and Helah—and the genealogy clearly distinguishes between their respective children. Ahuzzam belongs to Naarah's sons along with Heber, Temeni, and Ahashtari.

versions.summary: Ahuzzam is a person mentioned in 1 Chronicles as a descendant of Judah through Ashhur, the father of Tekoa. He is one of the sons of Ashhur and his wife Naarah, and thus belongs to the tribe of Judah. He is primarily known from the genealogies in the books of Chronicles.
versions.title: Descendant of Judah
versions.reason: [major] Ahuzzam is a person from the genealogies in 1 Chronicles 4, tracing descendants of Judah. There is no information placing him in the period of the united monarchy. Since he is linked to early lineages of the tribe of Judah, 'patriarchs' is more appropriate, although exact dating is uncertain.; [minor] The roles array is empty. Even for a person known only from genealogies, a role such as 'Descendant of Judah' or similar should be specified.; [minor] There are four keyEvents for a person mentioned in only two verses (1 Chron 4:5-6). The events overlap somewhat and could have been consolidated. Event 3 ('Naara as mother') and event 4 ('Placement in the tribal history of Judah') are actually context, not separate events connected to Ahuzzam.; [minor] The title 'Descendant of Judah' is correct but could be made more specific, for example, 'Son of Ashhur, descendant of Judah'.; [minor] Footnotes are missing. A linguistic footnote about the name Ahuzzam and a historical footnote about Tekoa would have been useful.

He is one of the sons of Ashhur and his wife Naarah, and thus belongs to the tribe of Judah. Ahuzzam is primarily known from the genealogies in the books of Chronicles, where he is mentioned in connection with the mapping of Judah's descendants.
versions.title: Son of Ashhur, descendant of Judah
versions.reason: [major] Ahussam belongs to the genealogies in 1 Chronicles linked to the tribe of Judah, but he is not a patriarch in the traditional sense. Chronologically, he fits better in the period of 'united-kingdom' or 'judges', since Tekoa was an established city in Judah. The period 'patriarchs' typically refers to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Since his exact time period is unknown but connected to settlement in Judah, 'judges' or 'united-kingdom' is more appropriate. I choose 'judges' as a reasonable estimate for the early genealogical lines associated with Tekoa.; [minor] Calling Ahussam a 'tribal father of Judah' is somewhat exaggerated. There is no biblical indication that he was a tribal father with his own clan. He is only mentioned as a son of Ashhur in a genealogy. 'Descendant of Judah' or 'Member of the tribe of Judah' is more precise.; [minor] The summary is somewhat similar to the previous version and could be improved with more varied wording and some additional context about his place in the genealogy.; [minor] The two key events overlap significantly – both refer to exactly the same verse (1 Chron 4:5-6). It might be better to combine them or make the second one more distinct.; [minor] According to 1 Chron 4:6, Naara's sons were Ahussam, Hefer, Temeni and Haahashtari. The sibling 'ahastari' should probably be 'haahashtari' (Hebrew: האחשתרי) to correctly reflect the full name.

versions.summary: Ahussam is mentioned in 1 Chronicles 4:6 as one of the sons of Ashhur, founder of Tekoa, and his wife Naarah. He belongs to the tribe of Judah and is part of the extensive genealogy that the books of Chronicles provide for Judah's descendants. Although little is known about Ahussam beyond his place in the family tree, his inclusion testifies to the importance of documenting lineages for Israel's tribal divisions and land distribution. His father Ashhur is linked to Tekoa, an important city in the hill country of Judah that later became known as the home of the prophet Amos.
versions.title: Son of Ashhur and Naarah, descendant of Judah
versions.reason: [minor] Ahussam is known only from the genealogies in 1 Chronicles and cannot be securely placed in the period of the judges. The assignment to 'judges' is uncertain. However, given that he is an early descendant of Judah and that the genealogical lists in Chronicles often cover the period before and during the kingdoms, both 'judges' or 'united-kingdom' can be defended. Retain 'judges' but note the uncertainty.; [minor] The summary is good, but the sentence about Amos and Tekoa, while interesting, may give the impression of a temporal connection between Ahussam and Amos that does not exist. Considering a minor adjustment for clarity.; [major] According to 1 Chron 4:6, Naara's sons were Ahussam, Hefer, Temeni, and Haahashtari. The siblings should therefore be 'hefer', 'temeni', and 'haahashtari'. The IDs appear correct but should be verified against actual IDs in the database. The list appears complete.; [minor] The roles are correct but minimal. One could optionally include 'Member of the tribe of Judah' for greater precision, but the existing roles are acceptable for a person with very limited biblical mention.

footnotes.text: The name Ahuzzam (Hebrew: אֲחוּזָּם, 'Ahuzzam') may be derived from the Hebrew root אחז (achaz), meaning 'to seize' or 'to take possession'. The name can thus be interpreted as 'possession' or 'the one who seizes', which may reflect a connection to land holdings or a desire for God's blessing over the inheritance.

Tekoa, the city that Ahuzzam's father Ashhur is considered to have founded, was located in the Judean hills about 16 km south of Jerusalem. The town is known as the home of the prophet Amos (Am 1:1) and the wise woman whom Joab sent to King David (2 Sam 14:2). Archaeological excavations at Khirbet Tequ'a have revealed settlement traces from the Iron Age.

In the genealogies of Chronicles, the expression 'father of' (Hebrew: אבי) a city often refers to the person regarded as the founder or leader of a settlement, rather than merely biological parentage. This pattern is seen repeatedly in 1 Chr 2–4 and reflects a close connection between family lines and geographical settlement patterns in ancient Israel.

Ashhur had two wives, Helah and Naara, reflecting a polygamous family structure that was common in ancient Israel. The books of Chronicles clearly distinguish between the children of the two wives, which may have had implications for inheritance rights and clan structures within the tribe of Judah.
